claim.pdf_says: 8.11 Intrinsic function names — page 243 column 2 ends with 'SUM' as its last entry. 'TAN', 'TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD', 'TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD', 'TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME', 'TEST-NUMVAL' are printed on the following page.
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:10886 — 'SUM TAN TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME TEST-NUMVAL' (six function names on a single line). Every other entry in 8.11 is one name per line.
claim.why_it_matters: Clause 8.11 is the authoritative list of intrinsic function names. Collapsing six names onto one line removes five of them from any line-oriented extraction of the list and mis-attributes them to page 243.

verdict.reasoning: Both quotations are accurate, but the difference is pure line-breaking / page-boundary furniture with zero content loss. Rendered PDF p.243 (printed folio 213): column 1 runs ABS..INTEGER-OF-DAY (41 names), column 2 runs INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE..SUM (41 names). Rendered PDF p.244 (printed folio 214) opens with TAN, TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD, TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD, TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME, TEST-NUMVAL, TEST-NUMVAL-C, TEST-NUMVAL-F, TRIM, UPPER-CASE, VARIANCE, WHEN-COMPILED, YEAR-TO-YYYY (12 names), then the COBOL-WORDS NOTE. Total printed: 94 names. The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:10804-10898 whitespace-tokenizes to exactly 94 names in exactly the same sequence — verified programmatically: identical sequence True, missing from md [], extra in md [], duplicates []. Nothing is dropped, added, duplicated, reordered, or altered in spelling. The 'missing' text the claim points at is present, on the very line the claim itself quotes, space-separated and plainly legible as five distinct COBOL words (TAN, TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD, TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD, TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME, TEST-NUMVAL). Clause 8.11 is a flat unordered membership list — its meaning is which names are in it, and every one of them is in the markdown. The claimed harm ('removes five of them from any line-oriented extraction') is a hypothetical downstream-tooling inconvenience, not a discrepancy in the transcribed content; the names remain trivially recoverable by whitespace splitting, which is the correct way to read a two-column list flattened into prose lines anyway. The residual page-attribution wobble (five names sitting in the page-243 block rather than the page-244 block, so the md page-244 section starts at TEST-NUMVAL-C rather than TAN) is exactly the page-break furniture the rejection criteria exclude: it shifts no semantics, and clause 8.11 spans both pages regardless. Falls squarely under two rejection criteria — the text is actually present on the quoted line, and the difference is only page-break/line-wrapping formatting.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The markdown transcription of clause 8.11 is complete and faithful: all 94 printed intrinsic function names appear exactly once, in printed order, with no omissions, additions, or spelling changes (verified by tokenized diff against both rendered pages). The sole deviation is cosmetic — the six names SUM, TAN, TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD, TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD, TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME, TEST-NUMVAL share one line at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:10886 instead of occupying six lines, which also places the last five in the page-243 block although they are printed at the top of page 244 (folio 214). At most this is a low-value cosmetic tidy-up (split line 10886 into six lines and move the last five below the page-244 anchor); it is not structural, and it does not affect the authoritative content of the intrinsic-function-name list.
